newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end firmer, budget response neutral.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end firmer, budget response neutral.

text.p: * Aggressive buying in Telecom, BIL turns NZ market around
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +7.63 at 2,410.15
372 nil * Volume NZ$69 million. Futures +8 at 1,218
Aggressive buying in Telecom and Brierley Investments turned the New Zealand share market around at Thursday's close but the response to the budget was neutral.

The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 7.63 points higher at 2,410.15 on turnover worth NZ$69 million. The index was hoisted off its 2,388.93 low by a surge of buying around the midsession but ended a little short of its 2,414.95 intraday peak.
Treasurer Winston Peters, delivering his first budget, said the surplus for 1997/8 was now projected at NZ$1.5 billion, against the $3.3 billion projected in March.
Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities said the market would treat the budget neutrally, even though it was not as strong fiscally as some would have liked.
"The surplus is at the low end of the expectations and following years' surpluses are down as well. But for the equity market it doesn't really matter that much," he said.

The buying around lunch time centred on Telecom, which ended seven cents up at NZ$7.11, and Brierley Investments, which firmed one cent to $1.39. Telecom was bid up from a low of $7.00 and reached $7.14 at one point, but the rally was not broadly based.

Auckland casino operator Sky City ended 25 cents higher at NZ$7.20 after peaking at $7.50. It earlier said Brierley was to buy out Harrah's stake at NZ$6.75 a share. Sky City would also buy out Harrah's management contract for NZ$13.5 million.
One of the biggest deals of the day was 3.3 million St Lukes convertible notes. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
